mapper.sql: SELECT b.id, b.schedule_id, b.user_id, stu.name AS user_name, c.name AS course_name, c.type AS course_type, t.name AS teacher_name, s.room, st.name AS store_name, s.start_time, s.end_time, b.status, b.waitlist_no, b.cost_hours, b.checkin_points, b.created_at FROM booking b LEFT JOIN course_schedule s ON s.id = b.schedule_id LEFT JOIN store st ON st.id = s.store_id LEFT JOIN course c ON c.id = s.course_id LEFT JOIN teacher t ON t.id = s.teacher_id LEFT JOIN `user` stu ON stu.id = b.user_id
mapper.insert: INSERT INTO booking (store_id, user_id, schedule_id, status, waitlist_no, is_admin, cost_hours, checkin_points) VALUES (#{storeId}, #{userId}, #{scheduleId}, #{status}, #{waitlistNo}, COALESCE(#{isAdmin},0), #{costHours}, #{checkinPoints})
mapper.update: UPDATE booking SET status = #{status} WHERE id = #{id} AND status = #{expectStatus}
UPDATE booking SET status = 'cancelled', cancel_deduct = #{cancelDeduct}, cancel_at = NOW() WHERE id = #{id} AND status = #{expectStatus}
mapper.select: SELECT * FROM booking WHERE schedule_id = #{scheduleId} AND status IN ('booked','waitlist') ORDER BY id
SELECT * FROM booking WHERE schedule_id = #{scheduleId} AND status = 'waitlist' ORDER BY waitlist_no, id LIMIT 1
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM booking WHERE schedule_id = #{scheduleId} AND status = 'waitlist'
mapper.update: UPDATE booking SET status = 'booked', waitlist_no = NULL WHERE id = #{id} AND status = 'waitlist'
